review_reference: Owner, 2026-11-13, Q74 ("if it's proven by 00:30 UTC, it goes to the owner to sign and ships with 0120"); to be signed by the owner.
evidence: Migration 0121_outreach_registration_read_once.sql (placeholder; releases right after 0120) plus its runtime-grants.sql lines. WHAT IT DOES: the two read policies on outreach.registration_cases (outreach_registration_cases_read, permissive; outreach_registration_campaign_read, restrictive) and identity.outreach_registration_health_ids_for(uuid[]) keep exactly their rules but evaluate the session-constant parts once per query instead of once per row: the session facility and outreach.context_allows(session facility, 'outreach.registration.read'); campaign membership through the new outreach.session_campaign_pairs() (the session membership's (campaign, facility) pairs, read as outreach.registration_campaign_member reads them: SECURITY DEFINER, STABLE, the same owner, search_path and EXECUTE grantees, copied from that function); and outreach.privileged_run_active('retention'). outreach-api's registration list stops repeating outreach.registration_campaign_member in its WHERE (the restrictive policy applies it; no runtime role can start a retention run, so outreach-api never reads inside one). Nothing else changes: the create, update, retention and resolve policies, the other functions and every grant but the new helper's. WHO SEES WHICH ROW: unchanged. On a database with 200,000 patients and 511 registrations, every session (organiser, volunteers, a volunteer removed from the campaign, a member whose membership is deactivated, another group's volunteer, a suspended group's organiser, a hospital nurse, wrong purpose, wrong facility, no session, retention runs) times every hid_* role, 10,440 results (rows visible, the list, the duplicate hint, the Health ID lookup, health checks visible, an update of each fixture row, Identity's registration read) were identical before and after 0121 (same sha256); the suite outreach-registration-read-once.integration.sql (96 comparisons with the pre-0121 expressions, 22 named cases) passes before and after. SPEED (outreach-day load test, 500 people, 5 volunteers, 200,000 patients, day at 30x speed): registration median 141 ms -> 55 ms, p95 612 -> 248, max 1,508 -> 420; at 500 registrations the list 1.9 s -> 11 ms, the duplicate hint 1.2 s -> 5 ms, the Health ID lookup for 100 registrations 434 ms -> 8 ms; no lock wait over 10 ms. LOCKS: ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on outreach.registration_cases for ALTER POLICY, NOWAIT, at most 5 seconds (55P03). OLD SERVICES: today's outreach-api (with the repeated filter) reads exactly the same rows. ROLLBACK: a migration restoring the two policy expressions and 0120's function body; outreach.session_campaign_pairs() may stay.
